text:
Sam K: Quick async standup for the canary gatekeepers — adding statuses below. What I did: kicked off 5% -> 20% ramp for rollout-rls-12, ran smoke tests against the routing layer. Blockers: small spike in retry errors from a subset of customers, investigating. Today: monitor for 30m, decide on 50% ramp.

Eva L: Saw retries too. I traced it to a single worker pool hitting OOMs during long sequences. Logs show kv-cache pressure. I'll push a temporary limit on max_seq for that pool.

Jordan P: Heads-up — I added a canary flag on the gateway to prefer model-variant v2 if v1 hits 5xx. This should reduce surface area while we diagnose.

Maria G: Can you paste the command you used to check the pool memory? I want to scrub logs for correlated traces.

Eva L: Sure: ```bash
kubectl -n inference logs -l pool=pool-7 --since=30m | grep -E "OOM|kv_cache"````

Sam K: Nice. @Dan I think infra autoscaler might be too slow to spin up replacements for that pool. Any tweaks? :thinking_face:

Dan I: Noted. I'm bumping scale-up cool-down from 120s -> 45s for the pool group. Doing a config patch now, will roll in 2m.

deploy-bot: [10:12 AM] Canary rollout started: rollout-rls-12 -> 5% (id: r-12-canary). Logs: https://internal.corp/logs/r-12-canary

Sam K: After Dan's change, if retries persist we'll pause the ramp and revert traffic slice to 5%. Keep alerts loud.

Jordan P: Ran a quick eval on prompt set 'billing-checks' — v2 looks fine, no regressions. Uploading results to the dashboard.

Maria G: I'm running a quick trace correlation against the retry window (10:06–10:09). If anyone sees elevated latency traces with kv_cache:true tag please ping here.

Eva L: Patch applied to limit max_seq=2048 on pool-7. Observing memory now.

Sam K: Update in 10. If stable we'll go to 50% at +30m, otherwise hold and run postmortem if it spikes. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
